title: Lab 05 — OTP Login: Single-Use Codes, Lockouts & Whose Clock Is It?

variants.hint: You logged in with the code. What if someone who saw it over your shoulder uses it again?
variants.debrief: A used code kept working -- anyone who ever saw a code could log in with it. Single-use means testing the SECOND use.

variants.hint: Get a code, get a newer one, then try the OLD one. (You'll need the resend cooldown to be over -- whose clock decides that?)
variants.debrief: Requesting a new code didn't retire the previous one, so every code ever sent stayed valid. Testing it needs the cooldown to pass first -- which only the server's clock can make happen.

variants.hint: What stops someone trying all 1,000,000 codes? Try being that someone -- five times.
variants.debrief: There was no attempt limit, so a 6-digit code could be brute-forced. The test that proves the lockout also has to prove the CORRECT code is refused afterwards.

variants.hint: The Resend button is disabled for 30 s. Is that the rule, or just the button? Ask the server directly.
variants.debrief: The cooldown only existed in the page's countdown; the server accepted a new code request at any time, so a script could spam codes (and SMS costs). A disabled button is a UI hint, not a rule -- test the API.

variants.hint: Codes should die after 60 s. page.clock can't help here -- think about which clock the SERVER uses, and what test-support offers.
variants.debrief: Codes never expired. Faking the browser's clock can't reveal that: expiry is checked with the server's clock. The /test-support/clock endpoint moves the right one.
